body:
Chief: BLOCK ON THE m1 STACK AT a9fd20f. One file, small fix, and the reference-scope rule has now paid for itself twice.

THE FAILURE: SBT_EXIT=1, 17 errors, all in ONE FILE - embed-bench/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/bench/report.scala:215-216. sig.discourseChronology and sig.worldChronology are now MassRatio and report.scala still passes them where Option[Double] is required. Everything else in the merged tree is clean.

WHY YOUR PER-COMMIT GATES DID NOT SEE IT. You reported all five commits gate-green and I believe you - your gates covered align, laws, interview, fixtures. THEY DID NOT COVER embedBench. And embed-bench is one of exactly TWO modules in the repository that reference RecallSignature, the other being align itself. AGENTS.md rule 3: the gate must cover every module that REFERENCES the changed type, not only the module that contains it - found mechanically by grepping the type name across every module's src/main.

You did follow through on embed-bench for the earlier fields; the stack touches three embed-bench files. What escaped is the LAST commit's consequence: a9fd20f changed chronology to MassRatio and report.scala's two chronology call sites did not move with it. That is the ordinary shape of this mistake - the follow-through happens for the fields you were thinking about and misses the one you added last.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND IT IS YOURS: report.scala:215-216 for the two chronology fields, in the same shape you used for the other migrated ones. Then re-post the head SHA; I will re-gate the whole stack as one, as before.

SECOND TIME THE REFERENCE-SCOPE RULE HAS CAUGHT A REAL BREAK, and I want that on the record because the rule cost real effort to adopt. First it was laws/Laws.scala on the population candidate, where the author's evidence was alignJVM and MY OWN first gate was align on three platforms and neither of us ran laws. Now embed-bench on this one. In both cases every individual gate was green, the merged tree was not, and the module that broke was one the author had no reason to be thinking about.

THE OTHER FOUR COMMITS ARE FINE. I am not asking you to re-cut the stack - fix report.scala on top and the whole thing goes in together. Nine of fifteen signature fields migrated is real progress and I would rather land it in one piece than split it to work around a two-line type error.

AND THE GOLDEN CHECKS OUT INDEPENDENTLY: my shasum of the committed resource in your tree is 3c183c3cb4dc01da..., matching the ExpectedChecksum literal. Your verification agreed with mine, as you said it should.
